1303.1228v2.title: Evolution Of Post-Impact Remnant Helium Stars In Type Ia Supernova Remnants Within The Single-Degenerate Scenario

evidence.quote: HVSs have extremely high space motions and can be unbound in our Galaxy; for example, US 708 has v \sin i = 708 \pm 15 \text{ km s}^{-1} (Hirsch et al. 2005).

The HVS US 708 (or HVS2) has a radial velocity v\sin i = 708\pm 15\mathrm{km~s}^{-1}, T_{\mathrm{eff}} = 44, 500\mathrm{K}, \log g = 5.23, and Galactic latitude b = +47.05^{\circ} at a distance of 19\mathrm{kpc} (Hirsch et al. 2005), giving a displacement of 14\mathrm{kpc} from the Galactic plane.
HVSs have extremely high space motions and can be unbound in our Galaxy; for example, US 708 has v \sin i = 708 \pm 15 \text{ km s}^{-1} (Hirsch et al. 2005).

The effective temperature and surface gravity of US 708 are consistent with our He PIRS models, but they require a subdwarf lifetime longer than several times 10^{7} yr to reach such a distance, if the SN exploded in the Galactic plane. Therefore, a less massive model may better match US 708, since less massive models have higher linear speeds and longer subdwarf lifetimes.
